findings: Verified as Wild Turkey (Meleagris gallopavo), family Phasianidae. The primary specimen matches the attached references and direct-source descriptions in its very large heavy body, long neck, small bare head, dark iridescent plumage, barred wings, rounded tail, long pinkish-gray legs, and strong anisodactyl feet.

The adult-male treatment is coherent: blue-gray bare head, red throat wattles, dark breast beard, bronze-green iridescence, and pale horn-colored bill. Both the primary head and detached head study have intact, consistently proportioned mandibles; the upper mandible projects slightly beyond the lower without truncation, reversal, or exaggeration.

The primary specimen is a single complete bird with one head, one beak, two anatomically placed wings, two legs, and one tail. The detached wing and head are clearly separated supplementary studies and do not appear attached to the specimen.

Wing and tail studies accurately show bold pale barring, rounded wing structure, and rusty or pale tail tipping. The closed tail on the principal bird is compatible with a nondisplaying posture; the text correctly limits fanning to displaying males.

All visible factual text matches the proposed research pass: common and scientific names, family, measurements, habitat, behavior, six field-mark statements, and all five palette labels are correctly spelled and ordered, with no duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical wording.

Measurements are directly supported by All About Birds: length 110–115 cm, weight 2.5–10.8 kg, and wingspan 125–144 cm. Audubon independently gives compatible rounded equivalents, including weight 2.5–10.8 kg.

The body-length ruler is internally consistent: 110 cm at the bottom, 115 cm at the top, exactly four evenly spaced unlabeled interior ticks forming five proportional segments, matching units and endpoints, and an explicit “SCHEMATIC – NOT TO SCALE” qualification. No conflicting marker is present.
Habitat, ground foraging, flocking, short flight to tree roosts, gobbling, strutting, lowered wings, and fanned-tail display are supported across the inspected sources.
